<text:style bold="true">Right Click</text:style>

The right mouse button gives the operations that make sense for what is under the
pointer. The menu is different for each kind of object, so it never shows what
cannot be done. Most operations change the kind of the object: a figure that is easy
to draw (a rectangle, a circle) becomes one that is easy to edit point by point (a
polygon, a path), and the other way is never needed.

<text:style bold="true">On an object (Select tool)</text:style>

A right click on an object selects it (if it was not selected) and opens the menu.
If the object belongs to a group, the whole group is selected.

<image:base64 col="0" width="44" wrap="none"></image:base64>

The menu of a rectangle: its only item is the conversion to polygon.

<text:style bold="true">Group</text:style>:

- Ungroup (split into its elements): the group is split into separate objects. It is
  the same as Ctrl+Shift+G.

<text:style bold="true">Copies tied to their parent</text:style> (made by Offset, Mirror or Array):

- Detach from its parent (make it an object of its own): the copy stops following
  its original and can be edited and moved by itself. It is the only item for these
  objects, because they cannot be changed while they are tied.

<text:style bold="true">Rectangle</text:style>:

- Convert to polygon (its sides can then be constrained): the rectangle becomes a
  polygon with four points; a rectangle with rounded corners asks how many points
  the polygon needs (the corners become short chains of sides). A polygon can take
  constraints on each side and corner.
- Convert to path (a smooth curve through points that can be moved): only for a
  rectangle with rounded corners; it becomes a path made of curves.

<text:style bold="true">Ellipse, circle and arc</text:style>:

- Convert to path (a curve whose points can be moved): the figure becomes a path
  with the same look, whose points can be dragged to deform it.

<text:style bold="true">Regular polygon</text:style> (made with the Regular geometric shape tool; its sides are kept
equal by constraints):

- Convert to polygon (its corners can then be moved freely): it becomes a plain
  polygon and the regularity is lost.
- Convert to path (a path with the same look, whose points can be edited): the
  constraints of the shape are dropped.

<text:style bold="true">Polyline</text:style> (open line made of segments):

- Close into a polygon (join the two ends): adds the last side and makes it a
  polygon, which can be filled.

<text:style bold="true">Path</text:style> (a curve with Bezier points, for instance the result of Vectorize or of a
conversion):

- Convert to polygon (its points can then take constraints; asks how many): the
  curves are replaced with the number of straight sides that you choose, so that the
  points can be constrained.

<text:style bold="true">Fill made with the Paint bucket</text:style>:

- Convert to polygon (independent of the lines that made it): the fill stops
  following the lines that close it and becomes a polygon of its own.
- Convert to path (a smooth curve through points that can be moved): the same, with
  a path.

<text:style bold="true">Text</text:style>:

- Convert text to paths (one curve per letter): every letter becomes a path, so its
  points can be edited.
- Convert text to polygons (straight sides, one per letter): every letter becomes a
  polygon. A turned text gives turned letters. After the conversion it is not text
  any more: it cannot be edited as text.

<text:style bold="true">Picture (raster)</text:style>:

- Crop (move the borders of the picture): the borders of the picture can be dragged;
  a click outside the frame confirms. Not for a turned picture.
- Perspective correction (move the four corners): four handles at the corners of the
  picture to straighten a photographed rectangle; the result is shown while you move
  them. Not for a turned picture.
- Flip (turn the picture upside down): the top and the bottom of the picture swap
  places, like a reflection in a horizontal mirror. The picture stays where it is.
- Mirror (swap left and right): the left and the right of the picture swap places,
  like a reflection in a vertical mirror. The picture stays where it is.
  Both can be undone with Ctrl+Z and keep the transparent colour of the picture, if
  one was set.
- Paste the pixels into the raster / Merge into the raster underneath (Enter): the same as
  pressing Enter on the picture (see Raster tools).

<text:style bold="true">Selection made with the selection tools of the Raster Tools panel</text:style> (rectangle,
ellipse, free hand, wand):

- Copy the pixels under the selection (Ctrl+C) / Cut the pixels under the selection
  (Ctrl+X): put them in the clipboard. The cut leaves in their place the Fill colour
  (the square behind in the colours at the bottom), the same that stays when the
  selection is dragged away; if the Fill is none the place is transparent.
- Fill the selection with the secondary colour (transparent if it is none) (Shift+Del).
- Modify selection borders (move the points of the outline): the outline of the
  selection shows its points (a rectangle or an ellipse becomes a polygon of straight
  sides). Drag them to change the selected area. Click outside to finish. To move the
  pixels, drag inside the selection or double click it.
- Convert to vectorial figure (a polygon): a vector polygon that follows the
  outline of the selected area. If the area has holes or several separate parts
  a polygon cannot hold them, so the figure is a path of straight sides.

<text:style bold="true">Rasterize</text:style> is the last item of the menu of every vector figure and of every group (also
of lines, arrows, polygons and curves, which have no other item): the figure, or the whole
group, is drawn as it is seen on the page and becomes one raster picture, in its place and
over the same objects. The opacity and the background of its layer are not part of it. The
raster is as large as what is seen of the figure, one pixel for every unit of the page.
Rasterize cannot be used on a raster, on a selection of pixels or on a reference object.

Operations that need several objects (Group, Merge rasters) are buttons of the panels, not of
the menu.

<text:style bold="true">On a point</text:style>

A right click on a<text:style bold="true"> point</text:style> of a selected polyline, polygon, curve or path selects the
point and offers:

- Remove this point (curve and path) / Remove this joint (polyline and polygon):
  deletes the point; the line closes up over it. If it is not possible (for instance
  when too few points would be left) the status bar says why.
- Convert the path to a polygon (its points can then take constraints), for the
  points of a path.

<text:style bold="true">On the empty page</text:style>

- While a polyline, polygon or curve is being drawn: the right click ends it (like a
  double click or Enter).
- While any other figure is being drawn: it is cancelled.
- With any other tool: it goes back to the Select tool.
- With the Eyedropper tool: the click takes the colour as the fill (secondary)
  colour, instead of the stroke colour.
- While choosing the reference of a gradient: the choice is cancelled and the
  reference does not change.

<text:style bold="true">In the panels</text:style>

- A colour (or material) of the Colors panel: Change color... (opens the colour
  window to change the swatch; for a material, the material window) and Assign as
  secondary color (dbl click) (the swatch becomes the fill colour).
- The two colour boxes of the bar at the bottom: Copy to button 1..9 of the Colors
  panel; each item shows the colour that the button has now. It works when the panel
  shows colours, not materials.
